title: Player visual audit — modern presidential workspace
recommendation: Refine the existing system. Correct misleading visual semantics and missing subject links first; then establish a clearer surface hierarchy and compose each screen around the situation, its evidence, and the next useful action.

findings.title: An adverse price rise is drawn as a fall
findings.evidence: In the oil-shock fixture, LNG reads ▼ +31.9% since the oath at 1440×900. The triangle communicates decline while the signed value communicates growth.
findings.cause: SIGN is indexed by valence, so bad always draws a down triangle.
findings.change: Derive direction from numeric change. Retain consequence as a separate color and explicit adverse/favorable label. Reuse the existing direction/valence distinction used by Stat and MoveText.
findings.acceptance: An adverse increase displays an up indicator and adverse consequence; a favorable decrease displays down and favorable consequence. Zero stays neutral. Verify positive, negative, and flat changes in both themes without relying on color alone.

findings.title: Page maps bypass the saved palette preference
findings.status: Source-confirmed; preference-switch visual proof still required
findings.evidence: MapView calls withDefaults(undefined) and supplies that default palette to usePalette. The existing BL-138 entry already records this defect.
findings.cause: Page maps initialize their own default settings instead of consuming the saved settings used by the player.
findings.change: Thread the existing persisted map preference through usePageMap and the map container's palette state. Keep map fills, keys, tables, and party swatches consistent.
findings.acceptance: Change each supported color-vision preference in Settings; verify a Nation party map, Courts map, their legends, and table markers before and after reload. Confirm actual canvas colors, not only a root attribute.

findings.title: Commodity identity and supplier connections stop at plain text
findings.evidence: Commodity rows have no category glyph. Expanded supplier rows expose a name, bar, and share, but no nation link. The project already has COMMODITY_GLYPH and supplier nation IDs.
findings.cause: These consumers do not use existing semantic identity and Door/route helpers.
findings.change: Render COMMODITY_GLYPH beside each commodity name; supplier identity becomes a flag/name link to its dossier. Preserve the selected commodity, sort, and scroll on return.
findings.acceptance: Every CommodityId has a rendered glyph with adjacent text. Open a supplier and return to the same expanded commodity and sort; keyboard focus returns to the invoking supplier. Do not link narrative shock text to an invented entity.

findings.title: Detail charts stretch like sparklines but lack detail-chart context
findings.evidence: Security's weekly readiness chart is a broad flat line with an elliptical endpoint. Commodity plots are independently fitted and lack visible range and date endpoints. Screen-reader summaries exist, but they do not provide equivalent visible context.
findings.cause: A 240×64 SVG with preserveAspectRatio=none stretches marks to any container. The shared Series API receives values without time labels; callers often auto-fit each domain.
findings.change: Keep compact trends compact. Extend Series with optional visible range/time captions and a non-distorting endpoint. Use a common domain for comparisons of the same measure and unit. Expose readable values through existing table/disclosure patterns.
findings.acceptance: At 320 and 1920, endpoint shape remains consistent; detail plots name unit, time window, and domain. Sparse/one-point history is stated plainly. Independent scales are labeled, and unknown observations never become zero.

findings.title: Repeated readings and quiet states consume the situation's space
findings.evidence: Security repeats 72% in its overview tile and a large readiness panel before reaching theaters. A short empty legal panel leaves a large unused column. The Record opens with a narrow feed beside an empty detail area.
findings.cause: Summary, detail, and absence are given similar panel prominence regardless of state.
findings.change: Use one authoritative headline reading, then a compact driver/history detail. Keep an explicit quiet-state message but let the related situation section use the released space. Preserve the Record's explicit selection behavior; give its empty pane a concise orientation and meaningful linked filters.
findings.acceptance: On quiet and active-war fixtures, players can locate current commitments and their causes without passing a repeated full-size readiness panel. Every previously available detail remains reachable. Do not fabricate activity to fill empty space.

findings.title: Surface hierarchy relies heavily on outlines and colored strips
findings.evidence: Dark Executive and Security use near-neighbor navy grounds, borders, and repeated colored top rules. Light screens use many similarly weighted white rectangles. Existing portraits, glyphs, maps, and formal documents are useful assets to retain.
findings.cause: Sibling and nested panels reuse ground-base, while status trim competes with subject identity and selected state.
findings.change: Assign existing ground tokens to explicit canvas, panel, inset evidence, and overlay roles. Reduce permanent status decoration; reserve stronger border/tonal separation for focus, selection, and raised layers. Keep shadows selective and text backgrounds opaque.
findings.acceptance: In both themes, page, panel, inset, selection, and dialog can be distinguished without reading labels. Status remains legible without a top strip. No blur or imagery reduces text/chart contrast.
